anomaly_def.Name: Database Memory Allocation Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Database Memory Allocation Anomaly: Excessive growth of buffer caches, plan caches, work areas, or parallel-worker heaps pushes total engine memory beyond the safe capacity of the host.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly: Physical pages and index structures on disk become internally inconsistent, leading to checksum failures, broken key ordering, or incorrect heap–index mappings.

When both root causes manifest simultaneously, the system may exhibit a mélange of symptoms: relentless OS-level paging or OOM kills interleaved with corruption warnings in engine logs; queries oscillating between slow full scans (triggered by corrupted indexes) and abrupt termination due to memory exhaustion; recovery or checkpoint phases that repeatedly crash or hang because corrupted pages are re-read into an already overcommitted buffer pool; and diagnostic utilities that report both cache pressure and structural corruption, making it difficult to isolate one primary culprit.

Causal interaction: (1) Runaway memory allocation reduces the headroom required for clean check-pointing and orderly flushes; an ensuing OOM or forced restart can interrupt write-ahead logging, heightening the likelihood of on-disk corruption. (2) Once corruption exists, query plans fall back to table scans, index rebuilds, or error-handling code paths that allocate large sort/hash buffers, further inflating memory usage. (3) The feedback loop of memory pressure → crash/restart → incomplete recovery → deeper corruption → heavier memory demand accelerates degradation, ultimately risking data loss and prolonged downtime.

entry.official_definition: Read timeout for X Plugin network communication.
entry.trigger_condition: A MySQL X Protocol read operation exceeds mysqlx_read_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The X Protocol network read operation times out.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL X Plugin system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when network data is not acknowledged, received, or written within the configured transport-level waiting window.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect packet loss, transport latency, client responsiveness, proxy behavior, and whether slow consumers or unstable links are delaying network progress.
